params.name: dem_rate
params.label: Demographic (population + aging) growth of radiologist work, 2026-2045
params.note: Christensen et al project +16.9% to +26.9% exams by modality 2023-2055 from population growth and aging alone (≈0.49-0.75%/yr) using Census 2023 projections. CBO's 2026 outlook has slower population growth (349M→364M, 2026-2056), so the centre is shaded down ≈0.1 pt.

params.name: dem_late
params.label: Demographic growth in 2066 relative to 2026-2045 rate
params.note: CBO projects population growth slowing to zero by 2056; aging continues to add imaging per capita.

params.name: util_g0
params.label: Per-capita (age/sex-adjusted) utilization growth, 2026
params.note: US CT use grew 3.7%/yr (adults, 2013-16) and MRI 1.3-2.2%/yr (2005-16); nuclear medicine declined. Christensen's recent-trend scenario spans -5.6% to +45.2% by 2055 across modalities. Work-weighted centre ≈1%/yr.

params.name: util_ginf
params.label: Long-run per-capita utilization growth (asymptote)
params.note: Growth in CT/MRI per capita has decelerated each decade since 2000; we assume further deceleration but allow either sign.

params.name: util_half
params.label: Half-life of convergence from current to long-run utilization growth

params.name: cmplx_g0
params.label: Growth in radiologist work per exam (complexity, images/study), 2026
params.note: Images per cross-sectional study rose ~10x at Mayo 1999-2010 while exams doubled. Work per exam (RVU-weighted) grows far more slowly than image counts; we decay this term with a 20-year half-life.

params.name: alt_max
params.label: Imaging displaced by alternative diagnostics by 2066 (blood tests, AI-ECG, genomics)

params.name: alt_mid
params.label: Midpoint year of alternative-diagnostic substitution

params.name: ratio0
params.label: Supply ÷ demand for radiologist FTEs in 2026 (current shortage)
params.note: HRSA (via Neiman HPI) puts radiology at ≈90% adequacy in 2038; compensation rose 6.6% in a year and DR positions keep expanding — consistent with a moderate (not extreme) current shortage.

params.name: ai_u
params.label: AI progress speed (quantile → timeline multiplier M)
params.dist: Regime mixture: 15% stall (M 1.6-3.0), 55% trend (lognormal, median 1, σ_log 0.25), 18% fast (M 0.40-0.65), 12% transformative (M 0.25-0.45, task ceilings lifted)
params.note: Loose guidance only. M multiplies the number of years from 2026 until each capability arrives.

params.name: cap_draft_T0
params.label: Midpoint year: reliable draft reports & automated measurements (M=1)
params.note: Generative draft reporting already gave +15.5% documentation efficiency on radiographs in a 24k-study prospective cohort.

params.name: cap_admin_T0
params.label: Midpoint year: protocoling, scheduling, QA and admin automation (M=1)

params.name: cap_interp_T0
params.label: Midpoint year: AI assistance that materially speeds interpretation (M=1)
params.note: Real-world meta-analysis finds no significant time savings yet; radiologists under-use AI predictions.

params.name: cap_consult_T0
params.label: Midpoint year: AI support for clinical synthesis/communication (M=1)

params.name: cap_proc_T0
params.label: Midpoint year: meaningful automation of procedural/physical work (M=1)

params.name: cap_width
params.label: Capability S-curve width (logistic scale; 10→90% ≈ 4.4×)

params.name: m_interp
params.label: Max time saved on interpretation by assistive AI (radiologist still reads)

params.name: m_draft
params.label: Max time saved on measurement & report drafting
params.note: Northwestern's draft-report tool saved 15.5% of total radiograph reporting time (up to 40% for some readers); if drafting/measurement is ~30% of reading time, that is already ~50% of this sub-task.

params.name: m_consult
params.label: Max time saved on clinical synthesis/consultation/communication
params.note: Langlotz: record summarization −30% tech/provider communication; non-routine communication −30%; patient explanation −30%.

params.name: m_admin
params.label: Max time saved on administrative work (protocoling, QA, scheduling)
params.note: Langlotz: automated protocoling −60% (30-70%).

params.name: m_proc
params.label: Max time saved on physical/procedural work

params.name: adopt_mid
params.label: Midpoint year of effective clinical adoption of assistive AI
params.note: ≈1,100 radiology AI devices cleared by 2025 but claims-based use was concentrated in a handful of products. Precedent: mammography CAD (FDA 1998, CMS payment 2002) reached most US screening exams within ~6 years.

params.name: adopt_width
params.label: Assistive adoption S-curve width

params.name: adopt_max
params.label: Saturation share of work done with assistive AI

params.name: ovh_max
params.label: New oversight work created by AI (governance, auditing, validation), share of time
params.note: Langlotz explicitly does not model AI monitoring/oversight time; this is the reinstatement term inside the reading room.

params.name: w1
params.label: Tier 1 share of interpretive work: normal/negative radiographs & screening exams

params.name: w2
params.label: Tier 2 share: all radiographs, screening mammography, standardized follow-ups
params.note: Langlotz delegation assumptions: mammography 50%, radiography 40%, other modalities 3%.

params.name: w3
params.label: Tier 3 share: complex diagnostic CT/MR/US/NM

params.name: tcap1_T0
params.label: Tier 1 technical capability year (not AI-speed scaled)
params.note: An autonomous normal-chest-radiograph product received EU CE Class IIb marking in 2022.

params.name: tcap2_T0
params.label: Tier 2 technical capability year (M=1)

params.name: tcap3_T0
params.label: Tier 3 technical capability year (M=1)

params.name: tcap4_T0
params.label: Tier 4 (residual hardest work) capability year (M=1)

params.name: lval
params.label: Clinical-validation lag (prospective, multi-site) after capability; tier-1 median
params.note: MASAI ran 2021-2025 from randomisation to primary readout. Tiers 2-4 multiply by 1.2/1.5/1.8.

params.name: lfda
params.label: FDA authorization lag for autonomous claims; tier-2 median
params.note: No autonomous radiology read is FDA-authorized as of 2026; the IDx-DR De Novo (2018) is the main autonomous precedent. Tier multipliers 0.75/1.0/1.5/2.0.

params.name: lpay
params.label: Liability + reimbursement + scope-of-practice acceptance lag; tier-2 median
params.note: Autonomous retinal AI: FDA 2018 → Category I CPT 92229 in 2021. Mock jurors penalize radiologists who disagree with AI. Medicare professional-component billing presumes physician interpretation. Tier multipliers 0.75/1.0/1.4/1.8.

params.name: ahalf
params.label: Hospital adoption: years from 'ready' to half of eventual uptake
params.note: Hospital EHR adoption passed 50% about four years after the 2009 HITECH subsidies; reimbursed mammography CAD diffused within ≈4-6 years.

params.name: awidth
params.label: Autonomy adoption S-curve width

params.name: amax1
params.label: Eventual uptake of tier-1 autonomy (share of eligible work)

params.name: amax2
params.label: Eventual uptake of tier-2 autonomy

params.name: amax3
params.label: Eventual uptake of tier-3 autonomy

params.name: amax4
params.label: Eventual uptake of tier-4 autonomy

params.name: f_sub
params.label: Share of interpretation+drafting time actually removed per AI-first/autonomous study
params.note: Residual human time: sampling QA, sign-off, escalations, liability review.

params.name: pc_share
params.label: Professional (interpretation) share of the all-in price of an imaging exam
params.note: ≈20% for MRI, ≈25% for radiography of Medicare global fees; lower where hospital facility fees apply.

params.name: pass_through
params.label: Share of cost savings passed through to prices paid
params.note: Fee schedules are administered and revalued slowly; commercial prices are sticky.

params.name: elasticity
params.label: Price elasticity of imaging demand
params.note: RAND HIE ≈ −0.2 for medical care; deductible shocks cut imaging alongside other services.

params.name: access
params.label: Turnaround/availability rebound: extra work per unit of radiologist time freed
params.note: Non-price rationing: when reads become fast and available 24/7, clinicians order more (ED CT visits rose from 2.8% to 13.9%, 1995-2007). Applied to the share of radiologist time saved.

params.name: new_max
params.label: New AI-enabled imaging applications by 2066 (share of baseline work, before capacity limits)
params.note: Opportunistic CT screening, higher lung-screening uptake (18% in 2022), coronary plaque AI (new Category I code), AI-triaged screening programmes, quantitative follow-up imaging.

params.name: new_T0
params.label: Midpoint year of new-application uptake (M=1)

params.name: new_width
params.label: New-application S-curve width

params.name: lambda_new
params.label: Radiologist labour intensity of new-application work vs a typical exam

params.name: iota
params.label: Extra follow-up work from AI-detected (incidental) findings at full deployment
params.note: AI-supported screening raised cancer detection 17.6-29% with flat recall; more findings mean more follow-up.

params.name: latent
params.label: Latent demand currently rationed by scanner/technologist capacity
params.note: CT technologist vacancy 19.4% and MRI 17.4% in 2025.

params.name: thru_H
params.label: AI-driven acquisition throughput gain at maturity (faster scans, auto-positioning)
params.note: Deep-learning reconstruction cut knee MRI time ≈44% prospectively; CT is already fast and table time dominates.

params.name: thru_T0
params.label: Midpoint year of throughput gains (M=1)

params.name: cap_invest
params.label: Long-run extra scanner/technologist capacity built in response to demand (by 2066)

params.name: um_max
params.label: AI-enabled utilization management (order decision support, payer AI prior auth)
params.note: Langlotz: order-entry decision support −3% (0-6%) of advanced imaging; Medicare HI trust fund depletion projected 2033.

params.name: scope_max
params.label: Reads shifting to non-radiologists with AI support by 2066

params.name: nt_max
params.label: New radiologist tasks created alongside AI (reinstatement), share of 2026 FTE
params.note: e.g. AI governance roles, theranostics, quantitative-imaging consults, multidisciplinary precision-medicine work.

params.name: attr_mult
params.label: Attrition hazard multiplier (post-COVID ≈ high end)
params.note: Attrition rose from ≈1.9%/yr pre-COVID to ≈3%/yr post-COVID; persistence would cost ≈3,100 radiologists by 2055.

params.name: slot_g
params.label: Trend growth in DR residency positions (before market response)
params.note: DR positions rose from 1,132 (2022) to 1,241 (2026), ≈2.3%/yr; GME caps limit sustained growth.

params.name: resid_gamma
params.label: Residency-position response to market signal (elasticity to ln D/S)
params.note: After the mid-1990s downturn, radiology trainee numbers fell to a 1997 nadir (3,080) and then rose 84% by 2011; medical-student interest tracks the job market.

params.name: fill_kappa
params.label: Fill-rate response to oversupply (applicant flight)
params.note: 2015 Match, during the last oversupply: 86% of advanced DR positions filled, 55 of 166 programs went unfilled, and U.S. graduates took 67% of matched positions.

params.name: resid_lag
params.label: Information/perception lag before the pipeline reacts

params.name: fear
params.label: Applicant deterrence from visible AI progress (max fill-rate loss)
params.note: DR PGY-1 applicants fell 14% over 2023-2026 even as positions hit records and still filled 97.6%.

params.name: fte_drift
params.label: Drift in FTE per radiologist (part-time, generational preferences)
